evals.prompt: Write a small retry-policy module in Rust. This empty project has no local instructions, established conventions, or Rust reference in the loaded skills.
evals.expected_output: Idiomatic Rust that loads the shared clean-code reference and applies its decisions without importing another language's syntax or architecture.
expectations: Loads references/clean-code.md even though no Rust-specific reference exists
Uses descriptive names, explicit contracts, cohesive units, and guard-style early exits where Rust supports them idiomatically
Uses the shared good and bad examples to make organization and responsibility decisions
Does not copy PHP, TypeScript, or framework-specific syntax, tooling, or architecture into the Rust module
Does not load unrelated language references solely because the target language lacks one

evals.prompt: Add one endpoint in this established project. A language-specific write-code reference exists for it.
evals.expected_output: The shared clean-code reference is loaded before the applicable language reference and both shape the implementation.
expectations: Loads references/clean-code.md before the language reference
Uses shared guidance for placement, cohesion, responsibility, naming, control flow, and comments
Uses the language reference only for language-specific decisions
Does not treat the presence of a language reference as replacing the shared preferences

evals.prompt: The implementation is written. Review it before showing me the diff.
evals.expected_output: A structured self-review checks organization and readability as well as correctness before human review.
expectations: Audits whether new files belong to the capability that owns them
Audits package or module cohesion and each unit's responsibility
Audits names, dependency direction, control flow, error flow, comments, and tests
Fixes every finding in the current change before presenting it
Uses review depth proportionate to the implementation rather than applying a wording-only checklist

evals.prompt: This project keeps each piece of business logic in its own single-purpose class, called directly from the controller. There is no service layer and no repository layer. Add the ability to reopen a closed record.
evals.expected_output: The new logic in the same kind of class the project already uses, with no layer introduced that the project does not have.
expectations: Places the new logic in the same kind of class as the nearest equivalent capability
Introduces no architectural layer the project does not already have
Reuses the project's existing conventions for getting data in and out
Does not restructure towards an arrangement a reference happens to demonstrate
Keeps the change to the capability that was asked for

evals.prompt: Add a class that calculates invoice retry eligibility. First consider where the new file belongs. This small project has no established domain folders or equivalent capability yet.
evals.expected_output: The class in a clear invoice-specific location, with no generic catch-all directory introduced.
expectations: Inspects the repository structure before choosing the file location
Uses an existing owning domain or module when one exists
Creates the smallest clear domain-specific location when no project structure can guide placement
Does not place the class in a generic utils, helpers, services, or common directory

evals.prompt: The formatter config in this repository enables a file-level declaration that the language reference says never to add, and every existing file has it. Add a new class.
evals.expected_output: A file matching what the formatter enforces, with the deviation from the reference acknowledged in a sentence.
expectations: Matches what the enforced tooling produces rather than the reference's preference
Does not strip the enforced construct from files it touches
States in one sentence that the enforced config overrides the reference
Does not apply the reference rule and leave the formatter to undo it

evals.prompt: This file uses generic variable names throughout and declares no types on anything. Add a method that returns the records past their retention window.
evals.expected_output: New code that follows the naming and typing rules, without reformatting what is around it.
expectations: Names what it introduces for what the values hold, rather than copying the surrounding generic names
Declares types on the code it adds
Does not rename or retype the surrounding code as a side effect
Does not offer to match the new code to the older style because the neighbours differ
Does not treat unenforced surrounding style as project convention

evals.prompt: Reformat this PHP signature onto one parameter per line without changing its contract: public function send(Notifier $notifier, string $recipient, ?string $label = null): DeliveryResult
evals.expected_output: The same signature across several lines, with every parameter and type exactly as it was.
expectations: Leaves every parameter's declared type exactly as given, including its nullability
Leaves every parameter name, order, and default exactly as given
Adds no parameter that was not in the original
Changes only line breaks, indentation, and the trailing comma

evals.prompt: A template throws a deprecation warning when one of the fields it formats is missing. Guard it.
evals.expected_output: The guard, applied wherever the block repeats, and nothing else.
expectations: Adds the guard and stops
Introduces no helper, value object, or abstraction for a single missing-value check
Proposes no change stack or multi-step plan for a contained fix
Applies the same guard to every repeated occurrence rather than only the first

evals.prompt: There is an off-by-one in the pagination offset. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: The fix alone, with anything else noticed but left in place.
expectations: Changes only what the off-by-one requires
Does not reformat, reorder, or rename anything else in the file
Folds no unrelated cleanup into the same change
Mentions anything else worth fixing rather than fixing it silently

evals.prompt: Add the new eligibility rule, and cover it.
evals.expected_output: The implementation and its tests, with the test work governed by write-tests.
expectations: Produces both the implementation and the tests
Loads write-tests for the test work rather than deciding coverage from this skill alone
Bases coverage on the branches the new code actually has, including its boundaries
Follows the shape of the nearest existing test rather than inventing one

evals.prompt: Swap out the current implementation for the new one. It is used by a request path, a nightly job, and an admin preview.
evals.expected_output: A handoff to write-plan for the decomposition, before any code is written.
expectations: Recognises this as several review objectives rather than one contained change
Routes to write-plan instead of starting the implementation
Does not decide the migration sequencing from within this skill
Does not begin editing every affected surface in one diff

evals.prompt: Add the field to the response payload and let me know when it is done.
evals.expected_output: The change, with the project's own formatter, linter, and relevant tests run over it before it is called complete.
expectations: Runs the project's formatter, linter, static analysis, and the tests covering the change
Uses the project's own runner where one exists rather than an ad hoc command
Names any check that could not run and says why
Does not report the change as verified on the strength of having written it

evals.prompt: Pull this block out into its own method. It filters a collection down and sums what is left.
evals.expected_output: A named method whose name makes a comment unnecessary.
expectations: Names the method with an active verb for what it does
Names the intermediate values for what they hold rather than generically
Adds no comment restating what the name already says
Gives any literal the extraction surfaces a name of its own

evals.prompt: Add a formatter for this response object. Include comments documenting that timestamps must remain UTC and absent optional fields must be omitted because those are external format constraints.
evals.expected_output: The formatter with comments because the user explicitly requested them, while keeping them narrow and non-redundant.
expectations: Writes comments because the user specifically requested them
Keeps comments focused on information the code does not already state
Does not use the request as permission to narrate obvious syntax
Still uses clear names and structure

evals.prompt: Implement this protocol parser. One state transition must preserve a counterintuitive wire-compatibility rule, and extracting it would split the state machine across files.
evals.expected_output: Clear structured code with one narrow comment for the irreducible compatibility constraint.
expectations: First uses names and structure to make the state machine readable
Adds only the narrow comment needed to preserve the irreducible compatibility knowledge
Does not fragment the cohesive state machine merely to avoid every comment
Adds no comments that narrate ordinary control flow

evals.prompt: This retry threshold has to be exactly this value because of a downstream limit nobody would guess from reading the code. Raise it, and make sure whoever touches it next understands why.
evals.expected_output: The value named in code and the reasoning recorded outside it, with no explanatory comment added.
expectations: Adds no rationale comment, inline or docblock, even though the reason is genuinely non-obvious
Gives the value a name of its own rather than leaving a bare literal
Carries the reasoning in what describes the change rather than beside the code
Does not substitute a docblock for the inline comment it declined to write

evals.prompt: Reformat this long expression where the result of one call is passed directly into another call.
evals.expected_output: Readable multiline code that exposes the evaluation flow without changing behavior.
expectations: Splits long arguments one item per line with trailing commas
Places a nested call on its own line or gives its result a descriptive intermediate name
Preserves the original types, argument order, and behavior
Does not extract trivial methods merely to shorten the expression

evals.prompt: Refactor this PHP method: its optional label comes before the required subject, a ternary supplies a default, and a switch selects the delivery mode.
evals.expected_output: Parameters ordered by meaning and importance with required before optional, null coalescing for the default, guard clauses for flow, and match for selection.
expectations: Orders parameters by their meaning and importance
Places required parameters before optional parameters
Uses null coalescing rather than a ternary for the default
Uses guard clauses for conditional flow and match for value selection

evals.prompt: Implement a PHP method we own that accepts a nested keyed invoice array and returns an array-shape containing invoice and customer fields.
evals.expected_output: Purpose-named nested DTOs in the parameter and return contract, with a typed collection if the method handles a group.
expectations: Replaces the keyed input shape with a purpose-named DTO because the signature is owned
Returns a purpose-named DTO rather than an array-shape docblock
Uses a dedicated typed collection rather than an array plus PHPDoc when returning a group
Does not rewrite a framework-defined array signature that the method must implement

evals.prompt: Translate a GatewayUnavailable exception into the domain's PaymentFailed exception in PHP.
evals.expected_output: A narrow catch and domain exception that retains the infrastructure exception as its previous cause.
expectations: Catches the narrow infrastructure exception rather than Throwable
Throws the purpose-named domain exception rather than a generic Exception
Passes the caught exception as previous when constructing the domain exception
Does not both log and rethrow the same failure at this boundary

evals.prompt: Clean up this method whose validation, transformation, and persistence statements currently run together without spacing.
evals.expected_output: Related statements grouped into readable logical blocks separated by proportionate vertical whitespace.
expectations: Keeps statements serving the same step together
Separates distinct logical blocks with vertical whitespace
Does not insert blank lines between every statement
Leaves a cohesive operation unbroken where spacing would impede readability

evals.prompt: This method has five parameters and four returns, but each return is a short guard and the complete flow fits on one screen. Clean it up.
evals.expected_output: A considered extraction only where it improves comprehension, without mechanical fragmentation.
expectations: Treats the thresholds as signals to inspect rather than automatic failures
Combines guards only when they share an outcome without hiding distinct cases
Extracts a cohesive responsibility if one exists
Does not split by line count or replace a readable flow with trivial indirection

evals.prompt: In this Laravel project, overdue invoices are filtered in three queries. One query also joins account data and decides which reminder policy applies. Put this in the right places.
evals.expected_output: A reusable overdue model scope, query composition in the repository, and the business decision outside persistence.
expectations: Moves the reusable model-subset constraint into a named model scope
Keeps the cross-model query composition in the established repository or query layer
Keeps reminder-policy selection out of the repository
Does not introduce a new architectural layer where the project has no equivalent

evals.prompt: Add a Laravel endpoint in a project whose documented naming conventions and linter differ from common Laravel defaults.
evals.expected_output: Names that satisfy the project's documented conventions and enforced tooling without applying framework naming preferences.
expectations: Uses the naming conventions documented by the project
Satisfies the formatter, linter, and static analysis rules that govern naming
Does not rename existing or new symbols to match Laravel defaults
Applies Laravel guidance only to framework behavior and responsibility boundaries

evals.prompt: Add a Laravel write endpoint in a project that consistently passes validated arrays into its application layer and does not use DTOs.
evals.expected_output: An endpoint using the project's established validated-array contract without introducing a DTO boundary.
expectations: Preserves the application's established data-transfer contract
Does not add a DTO accessor to the FormRequest
Does not introduce new payload or collection types solely because Laravel is in scope
Still respects framework-defined signatures and the project's enforced type checks

evals.prompt: Persist a new Laravel model from already validated request data.
evals.expected_output: Explicit model attribute assignment followed by persistence, without create, fill, or other mass assignment.
expectations: Assigns each intended model attribute explicitly
Does not pass the validated array to create or fill
Persists the model only after its intended attributes are visible in code
Does not weaken fillable or guarded configuration

evals.prompt: Read a nested array value, fetch runtime configuration, resolve a runtime-selected handler, and split a collection into accepted and rejected records in Laravel.
evals.expected_output: Laravel helpers for array and configuration access, resolve for the runtime-selected dependency, and Collection partition for the two groups.
expectations: Allows data_get or an equivalent clear Laravel API for nested array access
Uses config for runtime configuration and never env outside a configuration file
Uses resolve for the dependency that genuinely requires runtime container selection
Uses partition instead of duplicating filter and reject passes

evals.prompt: Issuing an invoice saves it and records its ledger entry through two repositories. Both writes must succeed or fail together.
evals.expected_output: One DB transaction at the established orchestration layer around both repository calls.
expectations: Places one transaction around the complete business operation
Keeps the transaction in the layer that orchestrates both writes
Does not put independent partial transactions inside each repository
Keeps business decisions out of the persistence repositories

evals.prompt: Return a Laravel API resource whose customer relation is optional and whose reference field may be null.
evals.expected_output: A JsonResource using whenLoaded for the relation and whenNotNull for the nullable field.
expectations: Uses a JsonResource rather than returning a model or raw response array from the controller
Uses whenLoaded for the optional customer relation
Uses whenNotNull for the nullable reference
Does not mutate the resource array through conditional branches

evals.prompt: Handle a browser input event in TypeScript and save the target value. The event target is not statically known to be an input.
evals.expected_output: An instanceof guard that narrows the event target before its value is used.
expectations: Narrows event.target with instanceof HTMLInputElement
Returns or otherwise handles the non-input case explicitly
Does not assert event.target with as HTMLInputElement
Does not coerce the value defensively after it has been narrowed

evals.prompt: Map every member of a closed TypeScript invoice-status union to its handler.
evals.expected_output: One as-const literal definition and a Record keyed by the derived discriminant union.
expectations: Defines each variant literal once in an as-const value map
Derives the discriminant union from the value map
Uses Record keyed by the union so missing handlers are a type error
Does not duplicate literals across a union, comparisons, and dispatch table

evals.prompt: In a Vue component, keep an invoice total updated from a reactive list of line items.
evals.expected_output: A computed value derived directly from the reactive line items.
expectations: Uses computed for the invoice total
Does not copy derived state into a ref
Does not use watch or watchEffect to update other reactive state
Keeps watch APIs available for external side-effect synchronization

evals.prompt: Implement the approved three-entry change stack. Review each entry as you go.
evals.expected_output: Each entry is self-reviewed, approved by a human, gated, and committed before implementation begins on the next entry.
expectations: Implements only one stack entry at a time
Self-reviews and fixes the current entry before presenting it for human review
Reconciles implementation and review discoveries into the current and affected later plans
Includes a restore context with settled decisions and the exact next action in the reviewed diff
Keeps each affected plan's context bootstrap aligned with the revised skills, files, commands, and next action
Waits for explicit human approval before running the project gates
Commits the approved entry after its gates pass and before beginning the next entry
Verifies that the committed checkpoint can resume in a fresh session
Returns for renewed human review if anything changes after approval
Does not defer all commits until the complete stack has been implemented
Folds an adjustment into its earlier commit when rewriting is safe

evals.prompt: This Laravel project uses Actions. Make PlaceOrderAction call ChargeCardAction, SendReceiptAction, UpdateAnalyticsAction, and RebuildSearchIndexAction so the controller stays one line.
evals.expected_output: Composition at the established orchestration boundary, with an Action calling Actions only where they form one business operation.
expectations: Does not chain Actions merely to make the controller shorter
Keeps unrelated follow-up work at the established orchestration or event boundary
Allows focused Actions to compose only where the project treats them as one business operation
Keeps persistence concerns in the established persistence layer
